Boundness check (Gaia DR3, both at HD 10647's parallax and RV): Gaia DR3 sky-plane velocity difference, corrected for perspective, 0.17 km/s against an escape speed of 0.25 km/s at the projected separation for the summed masses -- consistent with a bound pair. WT 50's own proper motion is a perturbed photocentre (RUWE 3.32).

sp_paragraph: HD 10647 (1 -> 3, WEAK): WT 50 (Gaia DR3 4912898156569562624, M4.0Ve, Riedel et al. 2018) is a co-moving companion 2150 arcsec away: El-Badry, Rix & Heintz 2021, MNRAS 506, 2269 (VizieR J/MNRAS/506/2269/catalog) (R = 0.0082), Gonzalez-Payo et al. 2024, A&A 689, A302 (arXiv:2407.20138; VizieR J/A+A/689/A302 table B4) (s = 37293 au, used as published) and Bertini et al. 2023, A&A 671, L2 ('a 0.2-0.4 Ms companion, WT 50, ... at 37350 +/- 29 AU'). CHECKED HERE: perspective-corrected Gaia DR3 sky-plane velocity difference 0.17 km/s vs a 0.25 km/s escape speed at the projected separation; RVs 28.15 +/- 1.08 vs 27.64 +/- 0.12 km/s; 0.18 pc vs a ~1.5 pc Galactic tidal radius -- plausibly bound, fragile. WT 50 is itself a pair: SOAR speckle 2023.66, 0.0296 arcsec, delta-m(I) 0.2 tentative (Tokovinin et al. 2024, AJ 168, 28) and a 2024 WDS measure at 0.10 arcsec (TSN 9001 Ba,Bb), with Gaia RUWE 3.32. INFERRED (orange, WEAK): Ba and Bb masses, Mann et al. 2019 (ApJ 871, 63) M_Ks-mass relation (5th order, no [Fe/H]) applied to deblended Ks: WT 50's unresolved 2MASS Ks = 8.609 split by the SOAR delta-m = 0.2 mag (Tokovinin et al. 2024, I band, flagged ':' tentative), assumed equal in Ks; distance from WT 50's own Gaia DR3 parallax 57.4584 mas. Ba: Ks 9.266, M_Ks 8.063 -> 0.175; Bb: Ks 9.466, M_Ks 8.263 -> 0.159. Equal brightness would give 0.167 each. Inputs: 2MASS Ks, Gaia DR3 parallax, the SOAR delta-m. SCATTER: relation 2.2%; delta-m dominates, +/- 0.01 M-sun over delta-m 0-0.4. VALID: Mann 2019 holds for M_Ks 4-11, M dwarfs. INFERRED (orange, WEAK): Bb's projected separation, 0.10 arcsec x 17.40 pc = 1.74 AU, one epoch of a fast-moving orbit. No component Teff or L published; left blank.
flags: HD 10647 is WEAK, as asked: WT 50 is 37,300 AU (0.18 pc) away. Three papers count it as a physical companion (El-Badry 2021 with R = 0.008; Gonzalez-Payo 2024; Bertini 2023). The 3D check supports binding: the sky-plane velocity difference after perspective correction is 0.17 km/s, against an escape speed of 0.25 km/s, and the RVs agree within 1.1 km/s. Such wide pairs are easily disrupted, and no orbit is measured.

HD 10647 DEVIATES from the +1 target: it goes to 3, not 2. WT 50 is a close pair, resolved by SOAR speckle in 2023 (0.0296", tentative ':', Tokovinin 2024) and measured again in 2024 at 0.10" (WDS TSN 9001 Ba,Bb, PA change of 106 degrees). Its RUWE is 3.32. If the owner prefers to count WT 50 as one star, drop the Bb row and set the count to 2.

HD 10647 Ba/Bb masses (0.175/0.159) are inferred by deblending WT 50's Ks with a tentative I-band delta-m. They are orange and WEAK. Ba/Bb have no Teff or L, so their solvent bands will read 'no luminosity on file'.
WT 50 is on 'Known within 100ly' as 'GJ 10246 B' (CNS5 naming). The Multi-stars rows use HD 10647 Ba/Bb, after the WDS Ba,Bb.

Projected separations use published values (Gonzalez-Payo 2024, or El-Badry 2021 / Michel 2024 where Gonzalez-Payo has none), not my own orange Gaia arithmetic (rule 4: published values are not orange). My Gaia DR3 x host-parallax values agree to within 0.2% (37329 AU here).

The young-association membership also conflicts with the Systems tab's 2.51 Gyr age for iot Hyi; not changed.
iot Hyi B is not the Unconfirmed 'iot Hyi candidate (PMa, a~18 au)': it is 8000 AU away and too far to make that PMa signal.
